name: Hydra clip-farming next steps
description: Runnable Hydra sketches for the PRACTICAL NEXT STEPS in hydra-and-clip-farming-techniques.txt. Each sketch's code is an array of lines; join with newlines to run in the Hydra editor (https://hydra.ojack.xyz).
license: Derived sketches build on Flor de Fuego's slit scan, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/).
how_to_use: Open https://hydra.ojack.xyz, paste one sketch's joined code, run with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter. For initScreen() pick the browser tab playing your stream. Sketch c3b and c2 use a small block of plain JS that the Hydra editor allows.

sketches.title: C1 - two screen-captured streams, cross-feedback
sketches.goal: Farm any live feed (YouTube/Twitch/webcam page) by capturing the tab and warping two captures into each other. No CORS fight, no ML.
requires: Two browser tabs, each playing a stream you want to farm.
Run the two initScreen() lines ONE AT A TIME so the picker lets you choose a different tab for each.
code: // C1 - cross-feedback between two SCREEN CAPTURES (simplest combo)
// Run the two init lines ONE AT A TIME; pick a different tab each time.
s0.initScreen()   // capture tab playing stream A
s1.initScreen()   // capture tab playing stream B  (or s1.initCam())
tweaks: 0.85 blend = trail length; lower toward 0.7 for livelier motion.
0.01 modulate = cross-warp intensity; raise toward 0.03 for chaos.
render(o0) or render(o1) to view a single farmed stream alone.

sketches.title: C3a - glitch the DEAD AIR (audio silence as the 'wrong' criterion)
sketches.goal: Harvest what the attention economy discards: react to silence, not action. Uses Hydra's built-in audio reactivity, no ML.
requires: Hydra audio (a.fft) listens to the MICROPHONE by default.
To react to a stream's sound: play it aloud near the mic, OR route the tab audio into your mic input with a virtual audio cable / loopback.
code: // C3a - glitch on DEAD AIR using Hydra's built-in audio reactivity
// a.fft listens to the MIC by default; route or play the stream audio in.
// a.fft[0] = bass energy 0..1. When LOW (silence), modulate is HIGH,
// so the piece glitches the quiet moments instead of the loud ones.
tweaks: Flip it: use a.fft[0] * 0.08 to glitch the LOUD moments instead.
a.setSmooth(0.9) softens the reaction; lower for twitchier response.
a.show() draws the fft bins so you can see the audio coming in.

sketches.title: C3b - glitch on BLACK / BLANK frames (cheap JS brightness probe)
sketches.goal: Detect cut-to-black, loading screens, buffering, dead frames with a tiny JS probe and glitch them. No ML, pure pixel brightness.
requires: Works with initScreen()/initCam() (MediaStream pixels are safe to read).
Cross-origin initVideo() may TAINT the canvas and throw - prefer capture.
code: // C3b - detect BLACK / BLANK frames with a tiny JS brightness probe
// No ML. Sets window.darkness (0 = bright .. 1 = fully black).
for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 4) sum += (d[i] + d[i+1] + d[i+2]) / 3
// glitch HARD when the frame goes black/blank (cut, loading, buffering)
tweaks: Raise the 0.15 for a more violent reaction to black frames.
Invert (window.darkness -> avg) to instead glitch only BRIGHT frames.
clearInterval(window._probe) stops the probe when you are done.

sketches.title: C2 - bridge ONE Scene Ripper detection (faces) into ONE Hydra param
sketches.goal: Make the visual content-aware: Scene Ripper's face detection drives the glitch amount in real time. The signature combo move.
requires: Scene Ripper side: run a small local WebSocket server that pushes analysis results as JSON containing a faces count (e.g. from person_count / face detection).
Hydra side (below) connects to it and stashes the count in a global the chain reads each frame.
Point Hydra at the SAME stream Scene Ripper is analyzing.
code: // C2 - Scene Ripper face count -> Hydra glitch amount, via WebSocket
// Scene Ripper pushes JSON with a faces field; we stash it globally.
s0.initScreen()   // the SAME stream Scene Ripper is analyzing
// more faces on screen -> more glitch (capped so it stays watchable)
tweaks: Swap .faces for any field Scene Ripper sends: object count, OCR hits, shot-type change, brightness, person_count.
Map to a different param instead of modulate: pixelate, kaleid, invert, saturate.
If no server yet, set window.faceCount by hand in the editor to test the visual response.
sketches.scene_ripper_hint: A minimal emitter: run a websockets server in the Scene Ripper analysis worker and send_json({'faces': clip.person_count}) per analyzed frame/clip. Any detection field on Clip/Frame maps the same way.

sketches.title: Decide venue early (gallery vs. online) - sets the legal contour
sketches.goal: Not code. The distribution channel decides your exposure to Content ID, DMCA, ToS, and privacy, so choose before you build.
notes: Gallery / installation / live performance = lowest exposure (no automated takedown surface).
Private link = medium. Public upload (incl. your own documentation) = highest: Content ID + DMCA act first, ask later.
Capture (initScreen/OBS) over scraping/.m3u8 ripping to soften ToS risk.
Strip or replace original audio to remove the most common automated tripwire (music Content ID).
Transform hard (the glitch IS the defense): fragmented, recontextualized = transformative use; reposting = not.
See clip-farming-tools-and-money.txt and the ethics notes for the full breakdown.
